message.content:
Let \(I = \int \exp(x)\cos(x)\,dx\). Using integration by parts, we get:

\[
I = \exp(x)\sin(x) - \int \exp(x)\sin(x)\,dx
\]

Now,

\[
\int \exp(x)\sin(x)\,dx = -\exp(x)\cos(x) + \int \exp(x)\cos(x)\,dx = -\exp(x)\cos(x) + I
\]

So,

\[
I = \exp(x)\sin(x) - \bigl(-\exp(x)\cos(x) + I\bigr)
\]

\[
2*I = \exp(x)*\sin(x) + \exp(x)*\cos(x)
\]

\[
I = \exp(x)*(sin(x)+cos(x))/2
\]

Therefore,

\[
\int -3*exp(x)*cos(x)\,dx = -3*exp(x)*(sin(x)+cos(x))/2 + C
\]

<answer>
-3*exp(x)*(sin(x)+cos(x))/2 + C
</answer>
